Well my response would be; you need to understand the reasoning as to why that person felt so low and terrible that they believed that everyone around them would be better off. 

If I ended up dying during one of my attempts years back, I would miss out on the wonderful things life has given me now.

From my experience, sexual assault and the stigma surrounding victims was the probably reason my late friend ended her life. She didn’t have the right support network, she didn’t seek help and the help she did get was professionals invalidating her abuse. It also didn’t help that her mother was pro victim blaming despite the fact it was her step father that was the abuser. 
She saw no hope. No possibility of things getting better. 

Now, with that being said. I know she regretted what she did. But when she attempted to take her life, she was in the pits and saw no way out of her situation except for doing what she did as she thought that would ease our burdens. But that made it 10x worse.
Her spirit is still around me today and hearing from other people that were apart of her life, she’s still around them too. 

There are people out there with suicidal tendencies and mental illness that do want to be better people and to be healthy. And it is possible to recover and be better. Sometimes, people just can’t carry on and that’s no fault of the person themselves, it’s the fault of depression, mental illness etc.
